source: Norton & Karczub 2e Table 6.1, PDF page 430 (printed p. 410)
about: Eleven structural loss factors, which the table heads with the symbol eta_s. The text that introduces the table (section 6.5.2) keeps the structural loss factor apart from the internal loss factor of statistical energy analysis: the internal loss factor adds the loss by acoustic radiation to the structural one, and a loss factor measured in air on a lightweight structure contains both, so these values are the material's own damping in a structure and not what a panel measured in a room would show. The page sets nine of the values as a mantissa times a power of ten, PVC's 0.3 and dry sand's 0.02 to 0.2 as plain decimals, and two of the eleven, sand and steel, as a range rather than a figure, which this catalogue keeps as a range. "Brick, concrete" is one printed row covering two materials and is kept as the page sets it rather than split into two rows this library would have invented. The table credits no source.
